subject: Redwood vs Hyperscaler: latency & throughput benchmarks — next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@globex.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood vs Hyperscaler: latency & throughput benchmarks — next steps

Hi Alex — really great call this morning, thanks for the time. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

What we heard from Globex:
- Primary goal: reduce p99 latency for realtime inference (customer-facing chat) and increase overall tokens/sec for peak windows.
- Current baseline: hyperscaler-managed endpoints; you're seeing tail spikes and higher cost at scale.
- Constraints: PCI-sensitive data for a subset of requests; need audit logs and deterministic performance for SLAs.

Why Redwood for this test (short):
- Production-first runtime focused on latency SLOs and throughput optimizations (continuous batching + KV caching).
- Ability to run A/B test against your current hyperscaler endpoint with identical prompt sets and measure p95/p99 + tokens/sec.

Proposed next steps:
1) We run an A/B benchmark comparing Redwood (configured with our low-latency profile) vs your hyperscaler baseline.
2) Test plan: 10k requests across representative prompt set (you can share sample prompts), measure p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, and cost per 1M tokens.
3) Connor (our SE) will lead the run; I'll CC him to coordinate test harness and credentials.
4) We deliver raw results + analysis and propose follow-on tuning (quantization/batching/autoscale policy).

Requested from you:
- Sample prompt set (10–20 prompts representative of production).
- A non-prod endpoint or short-lived API key for the hyperscaler baseline (or we can coordinate using your SRE to run the baseline on your side).
- Any specific SLAs/targets (p99 < X ms, tokens/sec goal).

I attached a short benchmark-plan.xlsx with the test matrix and metric definitions.

If this looks good I'll loop in Connor and Rishi to schedule the run. Best times for us early next week (Mon/Tue).

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

Attachment: benchmark-plan.xlsx (spreadsheet stub - test matrix + metrics)

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@globex.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Maya Singh <maya.singh@globex.com>
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood vs Hyperscaler: latency & throughput benchmarks — next steps

Thanks Marissa — appreciate the clear plan. A few clarifications from our side: 

- We can share a representative prompt set; attaching a small sample (see attachment).
- We do not want external parties given production keys. Can Redwood either: (A) run the hyperscaler baseline using our SRE-provided script OR (B) provide instructions and a harness we run in-house and post results? Option A is preferable if you can manage the baseline without requiring prod creds.
- Target: p99 < 350ms for the chat path, tokens/sec during peak window needs to be >= 1200 tokens/sec for the segment we care about.

We tried a quick preliminary run on the hyperscaler and saw p99 spikes around 800–900ms during bursty traffic (sharing globex-current-load.csv). If Redwood can demonstrate a consistent improvement at that load, we'd be very interested.

We can allocate SRE time to help run the baseline on our side Tuesday afternoon PT — would that work?

Alex
Alex Johnson

Subject: Re: Fwd: Redwood vs Hyperscaler: latency & throughput benchmarks — next steps

Marissa / team — I can take point on the A/B. Proposed runbook summary below (happy to expand):

Runbook (high-level):
- Window: Tue 13 Apr 2027, 14:00–16:00 PT (matches Globex SRE availability).
- Harness: our test-harness running on an m5.xlarge runner (isolated subnet), config attached.
- Traffic profile: replay globex-current-load.csv at scaled factor 1x for p95/p99 testing + short burst at 2x for stress.
- Prompt set: use the 15 sample prompts Alex attached and rotate through them to exercise typical token lengths.
- Metrics captured: p50/p95/p99 latencies, tokens/sec, failed requests, end-to-end cost estimate.
- AB methodology: alternate 1k-request blocks between Redwood and their hyperscaler endpoint to reduce temporal bias.

Initial acceptance criteria to call a win:
- p99 reduced by at least 30% vs baseline OR absolute p99 < 350ms AND tokens/sec meets >= 1200 for the peak window.

I'll also capture kernel/kind of model variant used (quantized fp16 vs int8) and any autoscaling config. I attached a short runbook (ab-test-runbook.md).

Connor O'Brien
Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
connor.obrien@redwood.com | (415) 555-0147

Attachment: ab-test-runbook.md (markdown stub - run steps and logging points)
